Spaces are windows: the Space row at the top of the sidebar is a window switcher (âŒ˜âŒ¥1â€“9); the tab list is this Space only.
Wordmark: Newsreader Italic. UI face and terminal face are both config keys (default IBM Plex Mono).

CHROMELESS â€” the default. Full-bleed terminal, a 4px hot edge where the sidebar hides. The localhost hook is a ruled chip anchored to the detected line (âŒ˜â†µ split, âŒ˜â‡§â†µ new tab). Attention state surfaces in the top strip, not as a popup.
QUICK TERMINAL â€” âŒ¥âŒ˜T drops a sheet from the top edge over whatever is focused (here a browser tab in the blue 'work' Space). Same 2px edge + hard shadow as the palette.
PIP â€” our own always-on-top window drawing a tab's texture: a video (left) or a terminal tab you're keeping an eye on (right). Signal band shows which Space it came from; â†— returns it to its tab.

TOKENS â€” what spike 4 renders from: paper/ink for both themes, six Space signals, ANSI 0â€“15 per theme, type ramp (IBM Plex Mono + Instrument Serif wordmark), rule weights, spacing, states, keys, principles.
Direction pass, kept for the record. Broadsheet was chosen; Aurora and Instrument are not being built.

SIDEBAR â€” third pass. Hover the left edge to reveal; hides ~300 ms after the mouse leaves; Ctrl+Shift+S pins.
Space row = window switcher. Pinned row. Compact rows (number Â· kind glyph Â· title Â· cwd/host); the 52px preview expands only under the hovered row (03) and under a waiting tab (02).
Footer: Space avatar + name + browser identity, shell profile row, assistant router row, + new tab / settings.

SETTINGS TAB â€” Ctrl+, opens a native tab. Sections left; key / control rows right (ruled segmented switches, boxed fields). Every change writes ~/.config/nus/init.luau, shown live at the bottom; the file stays the source of truth.

LOOK & FEEL — settings, eighth pass (proposal).
The nav gains two groups: LOOK (surface · theme · rules · cursor) and FEEL (motion · sound · startup). Every page: sections left, key / control rows right, a live proof on the far right, and the file it writes named at the bottom of the nav. Nothing here is a token change — Broadsheet stays fixed; these are the user's levers on top of it.

SURFACE — signal + ordered stops (gradient/aurora run through them), a family strip derived from the signal, base + tint, opacity (panes · chrome · window), texture (grain · stipple · stitch · linen · halftone; strength, scale, where), carapace style/width/radius/angle, aurora drift & breath. Presets save the whole card; surface.luau is the file.

THEME — the two papers' tokens with derived ones following unless pinned; contrast read out live; ANSI 0–15 editable or from a family; proof in a shell; import from Ghostty / iTerm / VS Code / Windows Terminal / base16.

RULES — the file is the page: syntax-coloured, a starter set (hue per tab · family per stack · by host · monochrome · time of day), a live sidebar showing what the rules do now, and a scratch call. A fourth hook, on_event, lets rules pick sounds.

SOUND — cuelume's seventeen cues, ported into the app as recipes (tone / noise layers, envelope, glide, shimmer) and synthesized natively; each drawn as its shape. Right: event → cue or quiet. Volume, quiet hours, your own recipes in sound.luau. MIT, credited.

STARTUP — the launch as a sequence: window (last · maximized · fullscreen · centered) → splash (draws in · still · none, hold min/max) → then (restore · shell · page · nothing) → atlas (planet · also at launch · persistent). Sound with the splash; links from outside; start at login.

CURSOR — shape, blink policy, colour (ink · signal · the tab's own · custom), motion (jump · glide · comet trail on the motion register), beam width; the pointer over the chrome; hide while typing. Drawn by nus, not the shell.
